text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Since Sweden joined the European Union (EU) at the beginning of 1995, people cheating with value added tax (VAT) by trading in gold have funnelled 250 million crowns away from the government. The gold traders have set up a company registered to pay VAT, gone to another EU country, bought gold excluding VAT, returned to Sweden and pocketed the money, escaping Swedish VAT. A court sentenced two gold traders to two years imprisonment and this will enable authorities to stop the fraud.
- This year will be a good year for Swedish banks, which showed pre-tax profits rising nine percent in the first quarter.

- Drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn's chief executive Jan Ekberg is doing his best to improve the group's development by presenting a string of measures to calm the share market after last week's news that the company failed to create growth and increase profitability.

- If the much critisised move to extend the period during which employers have to pay employees' sick leave pay to 28 days from 14 is scrapped, state finances would show a deficit of 1.1 billion crowns. The alternative is to raise employers' taxes by 0.28 percentage point.
- A slew of first quarter earnings report boosted share prices on Tuesday.
- Swedish forestry machinery group Sunds Defibrator winning a 500 million crown order points to a new wave of investments in the forestry sector.

- The budget proposed by the Swedish government last week stated that 500 billion crowns of public debt would be paid off during the next 10 years. The main thrust is to attain budget surpluses averaging two percent annually in the long run.
- Drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn reported disappointing performance for the first quarter of 1997 but promised to try harder.
- Electrolux, Sweden's white goods maker, disappointed markets even more with its first quarter results, but made no promises for the future.
